The unique 12-stage process of Dhokra making is the original creative instinct of the craft persons.
The process is carried out in twelve different steps as follows: Preparing vague model and coating it with first layer
बस्तर की परंपरागत धातु शिल्प निर्माण की प्रक्रिया कुल बारह चरणों में पूरी होती है ।
Cooling and finishing: The model is left to cool for 1-6 hours depending on the size.
The entire process can be broadly divided into five major parts as follows: Modeling 2 Moulding 3 Dewaxing 4 Casting 5 Finishing
सबसे पहले खेत से लायी गयी काली मिटटी में धान का छिलका मिलाकर गूंथ लिया जाता है । इस प्रकार तैयार की गई मिटटी से मूर्ति का ढांचा या कोर बनाया जाता है ।
A basic model is prepared by using black soil mixed with rice husk in appropriate ratio. Soft pliable dough is made by adding water in it. A basic model of craft is made and dried in the sun.

Black soil in the fields (locally known as chikti mitti) is brought and mixed with rice husk in the ratio - 1 kg of black soil with 100 Gms of rice husk. Water is added to knead it into soft pliable dough.
When the model properly dries, clean sticky riverside soil (locally known as rui mitti) is brought and cleaned again; enough water as well as powdered dung or wood coal is added and mixed thoroughly
Proportions are in the range 85-90% soil to 10-15% cow dung or wood coal.
The ratio typically ranges from 85-90% soil to 10-15% cow dung/coal.
When the model gets hard and dry, it is filed and shaped with metal files to bring into a proper shape. The pieces of dry sticky soil which have fallen are gathered, soften with water into a paste
The hard & dry model is filed & shaped with metal files to achieve a proper shape.
Fresh and 'semi' or 'sem' or country bean creeper leaves are brought, crushed by rubbing them between both palms till a green liquid oozes out.
all over the model until the models looks totally green. This is to prevent the soil from sticking to the model
The purpose of applying green liquid to model is to prevent the soil from sticking to the model.
हरी पत्ती रगड़ने से मूर्ति पर लपेटा जाने वाला मोम झड़ता नहीं है, चिपका रहता है ।
Bean Leaves (Sem Patta): Lima bean leaves picked up from the plants. Also, other plant leaves could serve the same purpose, but bean leaves are chosen, because of their high water content.
Lima bean (sem patta) leaves picked up from the plants due to their water content.

raw bee wax is heated in a pot over fire. The melted bees wax is filtered through coarse cotton clot into another wide mouthed clay pot filled with water. The wax cools and sets as it falls in it and floats on the top.
The molten wax is filtered through the cotton cloth into another clay pot filled with water.
पिघले हुए मोम को सूती कपड़े से छानते हुए पानी भरे बर्तन में इक्कठा किया जाता है।
Wax stings are made from the prepared wax; it is softened by leaving it in the sun. It is put through a hand held or standing press
in which metal sieves are inserted according to the thickness of the strings required

6. Making wax strings (Tikkal Banana): The prepared wax is softened in the sun and pressed through a hand-held or standing press (pichki). Metal sieves are fitted into the press depending on the desired thickness.
मोम को पिचकी (यह एक प्रकार का यंत्र होता है) में रखकर और दबाकर, मोम का तार निकाला जाता है ।
similar to that used by halwais to make sevaiyyan (called phichki pharni in Bastar, somewhat like a spaghetti press)
The wax threads are made using hand-held press, which is also known as phichki-pharni in Bastar.

When wax strings are ready as required, they are wrapped closely around the model, which is hard and dry and green with the application of sem-leaf liquid. When the model is totally covered with wax strings, designs of choice can be made with plain wax too.
7. Wrapping of strings (Tikkal Chadana): Wax strings are tightly wrapped around the dry clay form
A channel at appropriate spots at the bottom is made where the liquid metal is to be poured for casting and a pin made from wax is inserted in it.
जब ठोस आकृति बनानी होती है तब प्रतिमा का कोर नहीं बनाया जाता , आकृति मोम से ही बना दी जाती है।
Solid casting - Where a solid piece of wax is used to create the mould instead of a clay core.

Powdered sticky riverside soil and powdered wood coal are sieved separately through clean cloth. Mixed in the proportions 90-85% and 10-15%, water is added and kneaded to make dough like consistency and applied over the model.
Unrefined sticky riverside soil is taken and mixed with enough water and another layer is applied on the dry model. Care is taken to keep the holes or the channels for the metal clear.
Soil from the termite hill is brought, powdered and kneaded to make a smooth mixture.

a bigger channel or channels from wax are added to the earlier channels (for pouring metal) made at the bottom and covered with termite soil mixture to make the passage ready (inverted funnel shape) and dried.
On dry land a round pit one foot deep is dug with a diameter of 2 or 2.5 feet. The furnace can be square or a rectangle.
A round pit, about one foot deep and 2-2.5 feet in diameter, is dug on dry land.
After the soil is dry, wood coals is spread over it and at the bottom and light it

the model is then placed over it for firing. Wood is then kept all around and on top of the model and lights it. Wooden sticks are used to prop up the model to keep it erect. The pola or pipe is to blow on and to keep the fire burning steadily.
The model in the first furnace turns red on being properly kept in fire.

The model is held upside down for the liquid bell metal to be poured in the channels or funnels made at the bottom. The crucible is then lifted with long-handled pincers and the molten metal is poured in the funnel so that it can pass through the channel to replace the wax inside the model.
The wax inside the model is replaced by molten metal poured through funnel.
The model is left to cool for 1-6 hours depending on the size. If it has not cooled down, water is sprinkled lightly on it to cool.
When it is cooled down the outer mould is broken gently with a wooden mallet.
Wire brushes are used to clean the dried soil sticked to it and filed to gently rub and clean.
When the craft was not in its present commercialized form, the method of pouring liquid metal was different. It's still followed at many places in the interiors of Bastar.

While making the model, a separate pot filled with a sufficient amount of brass scrap is made. One side of the pot is kept open, which is then joined to the channel of the model and is fixed permanently with clay.

इसी समय सांचे के निचले भाग में विशेष रूप से बनाये गए मिटटी के कटौरे में मूर्ति के अनुपात के अनुरूप, आवश्यक पीतल रख लिया जाता है । अब इस कटौरे को मूर्ति के पैर की तरफ से उसी मिटटी से जोड़ दिया जाता है ।
When the model becomes red hot, it is lifted from the wooden furnace and turned upside down, which makes the liquid metal flow inside the model.
इसी समय भट्ठी में रखे सांचे को उलट दिया जाता है जिसके परिणाम स्वरूप पिघला हुआ पीतल इन सांचों से होता हुआ पूरी मूर्ति पर फैल जाता है और रिक्त जगह भर जाती है।
आजकल सांचे में पीतल रखकर मूर्ती ढालने का चलन कम हो गया है। पीतल को अलग क्रूसिबल में लेकर आग पर गलाने का प्रचलन लोकप्रिय हो गया है।

In conventional practice, Dhokra objects are small in size and are cast and moulded individually, but in the case of large objects, the segments are cast separately, then soldered together.
The common tools used are: - Chisel, - Wooden Mallet, - Hammer,
Phichki-Pharni (Hand-held press), - Pliers, - Tongs, - Wire brushes.
The primary raw material is brass which is collected from brass scrap or used brass utensils.
Bell Metal: It is a mixture of two alloys, brass and bronze, is used for casting.
Another furnace is made to melt the metal pieces ( 200 gm bronze to 800gm brass)
Meanwhile, metal pieces (e.g., 200 g bronze to 800 g brass) are melted in a crucible surrounded by lit wood coals.
Brass adds the shine to the surface, while bronze adds glitter.
Dhokra products consist of an alloy of bronze, brass, nickel, and zinc
In the metal arts, artifacts of copper and tin mixed metal are made, mainly in which statues of goddesses, idols of worship, idols of tribal culture, and home furnishings are made.
An alloy of copper and zinc that is harder and stronger than copper and more malleable than bronze or zinc.
An alloy of copper and tin sometimes containing small amounts of zinc, lead, silver, aluminum, or phosphorus.
Bronze is stronger, harder, and more durable than brass or iron.
Bell metal is usually composed of copper with 15-40% tin, but may contain small amounts of zinc, iron, or lead for damping.
The liquid bell metal starts emitting green blue flames, which is an indicator of the ideal temperature of its liquid state.
Brass being more viscous does not easily flow into the casts; bronze being heavy and less viscous helps in the molten mixture to flow easily and through narrow channels.
The pola pipe is then blowed on so that the fire is burning at high temperature, reaching almost 1000-1200° C, which is required to melt the metal pieces.
Air is blown continuously through the pipe to maintain the temperature (1000-1200°C).
And of course wax is indispensable in this process, since it conveniently melts out and burns, thus giving way to the molten metal.
Because of the closed system of dewaxing firing, it was difficult to reclaim the wax, which was either vaporized and burned or absorbed into the mould's clay.
इसी समय गर्मी पाकर मूर्ति में लपेटा हुआ मोम भी पिघलता है जिसे सांचे की मिटटी सोख लेती है ।

Rice Husk (Bhoosa): Husk obtained from the mills is mixed with the soil, to hold it together, as clay tends to break apart easily when dry; it also makes the mould porous and avoids the cracking of the mould during firing.
Rice husk is procured from mill. It is mixed with soil as clay tends to break while drying. It also prevents the cracking of mould during firing.
Wax is the appropriate medium for this craft because of its unique softness and malleability. It can be drawn out in wires of required diameters and can be moulded into desired shapes.
The Bee Wax is extracted directly from the hives available in the forests.
